name: SYSCALL_DEFINE1(rmdir, const char __user *, pathname)
prose: Generated system call rmdir(pathname) (namei.c:4652-4655): its only statement is 'return do_rmdir(AT_FDCWD, getname(pathname))'; getname copies the user path (an ERR_PTR from getname, such as -EFAULT, -ENAMETOOLONG, -ENOENT for an empty string or -ENOMEM, is handled inside do_rmdir through filename_parentat). do_rmdir (namei.c:4598-4650) returns 0 when the directory was removed, otherwise a negative errno: filename_parentat errors (path resolution, -ENOENT, -ENOTDIR, -ELOOP, ...); -ENOTEMPTY if the last component is '..'; -EINVAL if it is '.'; -EBUSY if it is the root ('/'); the mnt_want_write error (-EROFS for a read-only mount); the lookup_one_qstr_excl error for the child; the security_path_rmdir result; or the result of vfs_rmdir (which gives -ENOTDIR for a non-directory victim, -ENOTEMPTY, -EBUSY, -EPERM, -EACCES or filesystem errors). Before returning it unlocks the parent inode lock, drops write access, dputs the dentry, path_puts the parent path and putname's the name; an -ESTALE result (retry_estale) is retried once with LOOKUP_REVAL (it jumps to retry after releasing the path). It returns -EISDIR in no case in the code shown; a non-directory victim returns -ENOTDIR from vfs_rmdir (not examined here).
note: macro-generated function; packet name sys_rmdir does not appear in the file; set to the macro head at namei.c:4652. do_rmdir is at 4598-4650 and is outside the slice's start (slice 4611-4862 is its middle). reviewer round 1 right that -EISDIR is not produced by do_rmdir; the -ENOTDIR for a non-directory victim comes from vfs_rmdir, which I did not read here, so it is stated as the helper's behaviour with that caveat.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(linkat, int, olddfd, const char __user *, oldname,
prose: Generated system call linkat(olddfd, oldname, newdfd, newname, flags) (namei.c:5068-5073): returns do_linkat(olddfd, getname_uflags(oldname, flags), newdfd, getname(newname), flags). getname_uflags allows an empty oldname only when flags has AT_EMPTY_PATH (it then uses LOOKUP_EMPTY); a NULL user pointer fails the copy in getname_flags with -EFAULT, with or without AT_EMPTY_PATH, so AT_EMPTY_PATH permits but does not require an empty string and does not accept NULL. do_linkat (namei.c:4997-5066) returns 0 after creating the hard link, otherwise a negative errno: -EINVAL if flags has a bit other than AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW or AT_EMPTY_PATH (5008); the filename_lookup error for oldname (path resolution, following the final symlink only with AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW, LOOKUP_LINKAT_EMPTY for the empty case); the filename_create error for newname (including -EEXIST when it exists); -EXDEV if the two paths are on different mounts (5033-5035); the may_linkat error (-EPERM or similar protected-hardlink checks); the security_path_link result; or the vfs_link result (-EMLINK, -EPERM, filesystem errors). After vfs_link it releases the new-path creation (end_creating_path); if a delegation was returned it waits (break_deleg_wait) and retries when that succeeds, otherwise the error from it replaces the result; an -ESTALE result is retried once with LOOKUP_REVAL. On all exits it path_puts oldpath where taken and putname's both names. The names passed from the syscall wrapper are owned by do_linkat (consumed on every path).
note: macro-generated; packet name SYSCALL_DEFINE5(linkat) set to the exact head at namei.c:5068; slice 4863-5142 contains it. reviewers: round 1 right (a NULL oldname fails with -EFAULT in getname_flags, namei.c:157-165, AT_EMPTY_PATH only enables the empty-string case, namei.c:168-171, 220); round 2 wrong (NULL is not accepted).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(fsmount, int, fs_fd, unsigned int, flags,
prose: Generated system call fsmount(fs_fd, flags, attr_flags) (namespace.c:4377-4496): turns the prepared superblock of an fscontext fd into a detached mount and returns an O_PATH file descriptor for it. Return values: -EPERM if may_mount() fails; -EINVAL if flags has a bit other than FSMOUNT_CLOEXEC, if attr_flags has a bit outside FSMOUNT_VALID_FLAGS, or if the atime bits (attr_flags & MOUNT_ATTR__ATIME) are not exactly one of strictatime, noatime or relatime; -EBADF if fs_fd is not an open fd; -EINVAL if the file is not an fscontext file (f_op != &fscontext_fops); the error of mutex_lock_interruptible(&fc->uapi_mutex) (the mutex is not held then); with the mutex held: -EINVAL if fc->root is not set, -EPERM (with a 'Mount too revealing' message) if mount_too_revealing says so, -EBUSY if the context is not in FS_CONTEXT_AWAITING_MOUNT, the error of vfs_create_mount, -EINVAL if the new mount's superblock has SB_NOUSER (the mount is mntput first); then it sets the mount flags, cleans the fs context (vfs_clean_context), allocates a new anonymous mount namespace (alloc_mnt_ns; an error pointer is returned after releasing newmount via path_put) and adds the mount to it, opens an O_PATH file on the mount (dentry_open; on failure dissolve_on_fput and return its error), marks it FMODE_NEED_UNMOUNT and gets an fd with get_unused_fd_flags (O_CLOEXEC if FSMOUNT_CLOEXEC): on success the fd number is returned (fd_install), on failure the file is fput and the negative error returned. Every path after the lock was taken releases uapi_mutex before returning, and path_put(&newmount) is run on the paths from err_path.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(move_mount,
prose: Generated system call move_mount(from_dfd, from_pathname, to_dfd, to_pathname, flags) (namespace.c:4522-4600). Return values: -EPERM if may_mount() fails; -EINVAL if flags has bits outside MOVE_MOUNT__MASK or has both MOVE_MOUNT_BENEATH and MOVE_MOUNT_SET_GROUP; the error pointer value from getname_maybe_null for the destination name (without MOVE_MOUNT_T_EMPTY_PATH it is a plain getname, so a NULL user pointer gives -EFAULT and an empty string -ENOENT; with the flag a NULL pointer or an empty string yields a NULL name); if the destination name is NULL and to_dfd >= 0 the destination is the fd's path (-EBADF if the fd is not open), otherwise filename_lookup for the destination with LOOKUP_FOLLOW/LOOKUP_AUTOMOUNT per MOVE_MOUNT_T_SYMLINKS/AUTOMOUNTS (its error is returned); then the same for the source with MOVE_MOUNT_F_EMPTY_PATH and the F_ flags (-EBADF for a bad fd when the source name is NULL and from_dfd >= 0; the filename_lookup error). Finally it returns vfs_move_mount(&from_path, &to_path, mflags): the security_move_mount error, or do_set_group (MOVE_MOUNT_SET_GROUP) or do_move_mount (with MNT_TREE_BENEATH for MOVE_MOUNT_BENEATH) result. The acquired paths and names are released automatically (__free cleanups) on every return.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(pivot_root, const char __user *, new_root,
prose: Generated system call pivot_root(new_root, put_old) (namespace.c:4649-4731): makes new_root the root of the current mount namespace and moves the old root onto put_old, then moves root and cwd of processes that were on the old root. Returns 0 on success, otherwise a negative errno: -EPERM if may_mount() fails; the user_path_at error for new_root or put_old (both resolved with LOOKUP_FOLLOW | LOOKUP_DIRECTORY); the security_sb_pivotroot result; the error of locking put_old's mount point (LOCK_MOUNT, returned as PTR_ERR of old_mp.parent); -EINVAL if the current root mount or new_root's mount is not in this namespace (check_mnt), if put_old's mount or new_root's parent mount or the root's parent is shared, if new_root's mount is MNT_LOCKED, if the current root or new_root is not a mount point (path_mounted) or has no parent mount (the absolute root), if put_old is not reachable from new_root, or if new_root is not below the current root; -ENOENT if new_root's dentry is unlinked (d_unlinked); -EBUSY if new_root's mount or put_old's mount equals the current root mount. When all checks pass, under lock_mount_hash it unmounts new_mnt, moves the MNT_LOCKED flag from the old root mount to the new one if set, attaches new_mnt at the root's parent, detaches the root mount and attaches it at put_old, touches the namespace, removes new_mnt from its expire list, unlocks and calls mnt_notify_add for both, then chroot_fs_refs. All paths acquired are released by the __free(path_put) cleanups and the mount lock by LOCK_MOUNT's cleanup.

The packet item was marked 'dropped' with an empty prose, but pivot_root is a real function and is fixed here (the slice 4416-4670 includes its start; slice cut tail).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(mount_setattr, int, dfd, const char __user *, path,
prose: Generated system call mount_setattr(dfd, path, flags, uattr, usize) (namespace.c:5098-5138). Returns 0 or a negative errno. Return points: -EINVAL at 5111 if flags has a bit other than AT_EMPTY_PATH, AT_RECURSIVE, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW or AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT; then wants_mount_setattr(uattr, usize, &kattr) (5065-5096) is called and its non-positive result is returned at 5129: -E2BIG if usize > PAGE_SIZE, -EINVAL if usize < MOUNT_ATTR_SIZE_VER0, -EPERM if may_mount() fails, the copy_struct_from_user error (-EFAULT if the buffer cannot be read, -E2BIG if trailing bytes beyond the known struct are non-zero), 0 (nothing to do, without resolving the path) when attr_set, attr_clr and propagation are all zero, or a negative error from build_mount_kattr (-EINVAL for invalid propagation, attribute or atime bit combinations, plus whatever build_mount_idmapped returns for a userns fd: -EBADF, -EPERM, -EINVAL, -ENOMEM and similar). When it returns 1 the path is resolved with user_path_at(dfd, path, lookup_flags) where lookup_flags starts as LOOKUP_AUTOMOUNT | LOOKUP_FOLLOW, loses LOOKUP_AUTOMOUNT for AT_NO_AUTOMOUNT, loses LOOKUP_FOLLOW for AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW and gains LOOKUP_EMPTY for AT_EMPTY_PATH (kattr gets MOUNT_KATTR_RECURSE for AT_RECURSIVE); on success it applies do_mount_setattr(&target, &kattr) and path_puts the target; err is the lookup error or the do_mount_setattr result. finish_mount_kattr is called at 5136 on that path to drop the user-namespace and idmap references; those references are not dropped on the early return at 5129 (kattr then holds none unless build_mount_kattr failed after taking them, in which case the references are not released by this function).

The final remark about unreleased kattr references on build_mount_kattr failure is a reading of 5091-5093/5129 (the function returns without finish_mount_kattr); not verified in build_mount_idmapped.

name: netfs_read_to_pagecache
prose: Precondition: rreq is an initialised read request with rreq->start and rreq->len describing the region to read, ractl is the readahead_control or NULL (netfs/buffered_read.c:211-321, static void). Postcondition: returns nothing; the outcome is reported by setting rreq->error to ret with cmpxchg(&rreq->error, 0, ret) at line 320 (so a value already set by another path is not overwritten, and ret may be 0 even when the loop stopped early, for example for the zero-length case below). It loops while size > 0: it allocates a subrequest (netfs_alloc_subrequest; failure sets ret = -ENOMEM and stops), sets its start and len, queues it (netfs_queue_read) and asks the cache for the source with netfs_cache_prepare_read(rreq, subreq, rreq->i_size) (that returns a source value, not an error). For NETFS_DOWNLOAD_FROM_SERVER it computes the zero point zp (min of the inode's zero_point and the i_size, or the i_size for single reads); if the start is at or beyond zp the source becomes NETFS_FILL_WITH_ZEROES; otherwise the length is clipped to zp - start, and a clipped length of 0 logs 'ZERO-LEN READ', cancels the subrequest with netfs_cancel_read(subreq, ret) and breaks with ret unchanged (0 unless set earlier); otherwise, if rreq->netfs_ops->prepare_read exists, it is called and a negative result becomes ret, cancels the subrequest and breaks. FILL_WITH_ZEROES and READ_FROM_CACHE go to issue; any other source logs 'Unexpected read source', WARNs, cancels the subrequest and breaks. At issue, netfs_prepare_read_iterator(subreq, ractl) is called: a negative result is ret, the subrequest is cancelled and the loop breaks; otherwise start/size advance by the slice, NETFS_RREQ_ALL_QUEUED is set once size <= 0, netfs_issue_read is called, the loop waits if NETFS_RREQ_PAUSE is set, breaks if NETFS_RREQ_FAILED is set, and yields. After the loop, if size is still > 0 it sets NETFS_RREQ_ALL_QUEUED and wakes the collector.
note: slice cut head (function at 211-321, slice 1-259). reviewers: original right (the zero-length path breaks with ret unchanged, 250-256); round 2 right (netfs_prepare_read_iterator failure at 291-296); round 15 wrong: line 262 calls rreq->netfs_ops->prepare_read(subreq), whose negative return is stored in ret (263-266); the cache call at 235 is a different call (netfs_cache_prepare_read returning a source).

name: nfs4_have_delegation
prose: Precondition: inode is a valid NFS inode; type is an fmode_t (only the FMODE_READ and FMODE_WRITE bits are used) and flags holds NFS_DELEGATION_FLAG_* modifiers (delegation.c:144-147, int). Postcondition: returns nfs4_do_check_delegation(inode, type, flags, true) (115-134), i.e. 1 or 0. Under rcu_read_lock it reads NFS_I(inode)->delegation; if that delegation exists, grants all the requested mode bits (delegation->type & type == type), and is neither revoked nor returning, it sets NFS_DELEGATION_REFERENCED on it (because mark is true) and the result is 1, except that if flags has NFS_DELEGATION_FLAG_TIME and the delegation lacks NFS_DELEGATION_DELEGTIME the result is 0 (the delegation was already marked referenced by then). Otherwise (no delegation, wrong type, revoked or returning) it returns 0 and marks nothing. So the function can return 0 and still have set the REFERENCED flag, when the TIME flag was requested and the delegation has no delegated timestamps.

name: nfs_do_lookup_revalidate
prose: Precondition: dir is the parent directory inode, name the looked-up name, dentry a dcache hit (positive or negative) and flags the LOOKUP_* flags, possibly including LOOKUP_RCU (nfs/dir.c:1739-1789, static int, the d_revalidate worker). Postcondition: returns 1 when the dentry is still valid, 0 when it must be invalidated and looked up again, or a negative errno, notably -ECHILD to ask the VFS to retry outside RCU mode. It counts NFSIOS_DENTRYREVALIDATE. Cases: (1) negative dentry (no inode): returns nfs_lookup_revalidate_negative (1659-1669): 1 if the negative entry needs no revalidation, -ECHILD under LOOKUP_RCU when it does, else 0, passed through nfs_lookup_revalidate_done with a NULL inode. (2) dud (bad) inode, or LOOKUP_RENAME_TARGET with d_count < 2 on a case-insensitive server: goto out_bad. (3) a delegated verifier: sets the verifier to the directory's saved change attribute and returns nfs_lookup_revalidate_done(..., 1) (which returns 1). (4) If neither LOOKUP_EXCL nor LOOKUP_REVAL is set and nfs_check_verifier says the parent's change attribute still matches: nfs_lookup_verify_inode(inode, flags) decides: a non-zero error (marking the directory for revalidation with nfs_mark_dir_for_revalidate only when it is -ESTALE, 1769-1770) goes to out_bad, zero goes to out_valid (returns done(..., 1)). (5) Otherwise, under LOOKUP_RCU it returns -ECHILD (1777); an NFS_STALE inode goes to out_bad; otherwise it returns nfs_lookup_revalidate_dentry (1679-1725): a server lookup that must return the same file handle as the cached inode and a successful inode refresh gives 1, ENOMEM from allocation or a lookup error is passed to the done helper, a changed file handle or failed refresh gives 0 (and, if the directory's change attribute matched, the directory is marked for revalidation). out_bad returns -ECHILD under LOOKUP_RCU (1787) and otherwise done(error) with error 0 unless it was set by the verify step. nfs_lookup_revalidate_done maps its argument: 1 stays 1; -ETIMEDOUT becomes 1 for a root dentry or with the softreval mount option; -ESTALE and -ENOENT become 0; any other value stays; and when the dentry has an inode and is a root (IS_ROOT) any non-1 result except those already handled above is turned into 1 (a root of a disconnected tree is never invalidated). The -ECHILD returns at 1777 and 1787 bypass that root conversion.
note: slice cut head (function at 1739-1789, slice 1574-1826). reviewers: original right (bad or stale root dentries end up returning 1 via nfs_lookup_revalidate_done, dir.c:1650-1651); round 2 right (only the -ESTALE from nfs_lookup_verify_inode marks the directory, 1769-1770; a server -ESTALE becomes 0 in revalidate_done 1639-1641); round 15 right (the -ECHILD returns at 1777 and 1787 do not pass through the root conversion).

name: nfs_file_direct_write
prose: Precondition: iocb and iter describe a direct (O_DIRECT, or swap when swap is true) write on an NFS file; the caller holds no nfs_direct_req (nfs/direct.c:988-1079, ssize_t nfs_file_direct_write(struct kiocb *iocb, struct iov_iter *iter, bool swap); the packet name nfs_direct_write does not exist). Postcondition: returns a byte count written (> 0), 0, or a negative errno. Return points: result at line 1009 if generic_write_checks (or, for swap, the iterator count) is <= 0 (that value, nothing else done); otherwise 'return result' at 1078. Steps: count = result, adds NFSIOS_DIRECTWRITTENBYTES, accounts task IO, allocates an nfs_direct_req (-ENOMEM if it fails, jump to out), which starts with two references (kref_init plus kref_get in nfs_direct_req_alloc), takes the open context and a lock context (a failure result PTR_ERR(l_ctx) releases the request once and then, at out_release, a second time, so both references are dropped), records the iocb for asynchronous writes. For swap it calls nfs_direct_write_schedule_iovec(dreq, iter, pos, FLUSH_STABLE); otherwise nfs_start_io_direct(inode) (non-zero: release one dreq reference that schedule would have consumed, goto out_release returning that error), nfs_direct_write_schedule_iovec with FLUSH_COND_STABLE, invalidate_inode_pages2_range over the written page range if the mapping has pages, and nfs_end_io_direct. If the scheduled byte count requested is > 0 it waits with nfs_direct_wait(dreq): a positive result advances iocb->ki_pos by that many bytes and calls generic_write_sync (its return value is ignored), then the iterator is reverted by the unwritten part (requested after subtracting result); the returned result is the wait result (bytes written, 0 or a negative error). If nothing was scheduled, result is the (zero or negative) value of requested. Finally nfs_fscache_invalidate(inode, FSCACHE_INVAL_DIO_WRITE) is called, then out_release drops a dreq reference and returns result.
note: item named nfs_direct_write (dropped, not in slice); the real function is nfs_file_direct_write (direct.c:988-1079) and the slice 1013-1104 is its tail (slice cut head); FIXED per rule 6. The earlier prose omitted the early return of the generic_write_checks result and the double dreq release on the lock-context failure path (which matches the two initial references, direct.c:193-194).

name: nfs_parse_source
prose: Precondition: fc is a valid fs_context whose nfs_fs_context is reachable via nfs_fc2context, fc->source is the device name string (NULL or NUL-terminated), maxnamlen and maxpathlen are the maximum hostname and export-path lengths; ctx->nfs_server.hostname is NULL or a heap allocation owned by ctx (nfs/fs_context.c:1064-1127, static int nfs_parse_source(struct fs_context *fc, size_t maxnamlen, size_t maxpathlen); the packet name nfs_parse_dev_name does not exist and the packet's 'dev_name' parameter is the local variable fc->source). Postcondition: returns 0 on success, after kfree of any previous ctx->nfs_server.hostname and storing a new NUL-terminated copy of the host part (kmemdup_nul) and, in ctx->nfs_server.export_path, a new copy of the text after the ':' (any previous export_path is overwritten without being freed here). Return points: -EINVAL at 1073 if fc->source is NULL or empty (nothing recorded in fc); -EINVAL via nfs_invalf (1117) if the name is not host:path or [host]:path (no ':' at all, or a '[' not followed by a ']' that is immediately followed by ':'), with hostname unchanged; -ENAMETOOLONG (1123) if the host part is longer than maxnamlen (hostname unchanged), and -ENAMETOOLONG (1126) if the path is longer than maxpathlen (the hostname has already been replaced by the new allocation); -ENOMEM (1120) if kmemdup_nul of the hostname fails (the old hostname was already freed and ctx->nfs_server.hostname is NULL) or of the export path fails (hostname is the new copy and export_path is NULL); and 0 at 1114 after trace_nfs_mount_path. In the non-bracket form a ',' within the host part truncates the hostname there (host lists are not supported). The caller frees nfs_server.hostname in all cases (comment at 1102).
note: packet name nfs_parse_dev_name does not exist; the slice 1072-1326 starts inside nfs_parse_source (fs_context.c:1064-1127, slice cut head) and continues into nfs23_parse_monolithic; the described function is nfs_parse_source. Earlier prose was essentially right but used a wrong name/signature and said export_path 'unchanged' on length errors; the old export_path pointer is also overwritten without kfree on success (1109), noted.

name: _nfs42_proc_llseek
prose: Precondition: filep is an open file on an NFS inode, lock is a valid nfs_lock_context belonging to filep's open context (it is dereferenced for lock->open_context), offset is the seek offset and whence is SEEK_DATA or SEEK_HOLE (nfs/nfs42proc.c:869-916, static loff_t). Postcondition: returns the new file position (set in filep with vfs_setpos) or a negative error value. Return points: -ENOTSUPP at 889 if the server is not marked NFS_CAP_SEEK-capable (a capability check done here, not a caller requirement); the status of nfs4_set_rw_stateid at 896 (an -EAGAIN is converted to -NFS4ERR_BAD_STATEID); the error of nfs_filemap_write_and_wait_range(inode->i_mapping, offset, LLONG_MAX) at 902 (dirty data from offset onward is written back and waited on before the RPC); the status of the SEEK RPC (nfs4_call_sync with args.sa_what = NFS4_CONTENT_HOLE for SEEK_HOLE and NFS4_CONTENT_DATA otherwise) at 910, with NFS_CAP_SEEK cleared on the server when that status is -ENOTSUPP; -NFS4ERR_NXIO at 913 if whence is SEEK_DATA and the server reports sr_eof; otherwise vfs_setpos(filep, res.sr_offset, inode->i_sb->s_maxbytes) at 915, which stores the position in filep->f_pos and returns it, or -EINVAL if the offset is negative or above s_maxbytes. The function takes no lock and no reference itself.

name: nfs4_open_recover_helper
prose: Precondition: opendata is a valid recovery nfs4_opendata whose opendata->state points to the nfs4_state being recovered, fmode is the single open mode (read, write or both) to recover (nfs/nfs4proc.c:2241-2267, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. Return points: 0 at line 2250 without any RPC if nfs4_mode_match_open_stateid(opendata->state, fmode) is false (no open stateid of that mode to recover); the nonzero result of _nfs4_recover_proc_open(opendata) at 2259 (the OPEN RPC), returned directly with no nfs4_close_state; PTR_ERR(newstate) at 2262 if nfs4_opendata_to_nfs4_state returns an error pointer (again without nfs4_close_state); and 'return ret' at 2266. Before the RPC it sets o_arg.fmode and share_access (from nfs4_map_atomic_open_share), zeroes o_res and c_res and re-initialises the result structure. After a successful RPC and state lookup it sets ret = -ESTALE if the state returned is not the same state as opendata->state, then always calls nfs4_close_state(newstate, fmode) for that returned state, and returns ret (0 when the state matches, -ESTALE otherwise). The nfs4_close_state call is made only on the path that reaches line 2265, not on the earlier error returns.
note: slice cut head (function at 2241-2267, slice 2065-2335). reviewers: original right (0 is returned when the mode does not match, 2249-2250); round 15 right (the RPC error and ERR_PTR returns at 2259 and 2262 skip nfs4_close_state).

name: nfs4_select_rw_stateid
prose: Precondition: state is an nfs4_state; fmode is the I/O mode needed; l_ctx is a lock context or NULL; dst points to storage for the chosen nfs4_stateid; cred is NULL or points to a const struct cred * that will receive the credential (nfs/nfs4state.c:1033-1063). Postcondition: returns 0 with *dst filled, or a negative errno. Return paths: -EIO at line 1040 if nfs4_valid_open_stateid(state) is false (dst and *cred untouched); otherwise *cred is set to NULL (if cred non-NULL) and nfs4_copy_lock_stateid(dst, state, l_ctx) is tried (0 and *dst set when a lock stateid for the owner exists and is initialised; -ENOENT when there is no usable lock state; -EIO when the lock state was lost). If that gives -EIO it goes to out without considering delegations, returning -EIO. Otherwise a delegation stateid is tried (nfs4_copy_delegation_stateid, which may also set *cred): if one was copied the result is 0 and the delegation stateid replaces the lock stateid in *dst. Otherwise, if the lock lookup did not return -ENOENT (i.e. it returned 0) the lock stateid already in *dst is used and 0 is returned; otherwise (no lock state, no delegation) the open stateid is copied (nfs4_copy_open_stateid) and the result is 0, or -EAGAIN if that copy fails. At out, if the server has NFS_CAP_STATEID_NFSV41, dst->seqid is set to 0; the function then returns ret (line 1062). The success path with only an open stateid therefore returns 0 and *dst holds the open stateid.
note: slice cut head (function at 1033-1063, slice 1029-1283). reviewers: original right (an invalid open stateid returns -EIO at 1040 before dst is written); round 2 right (the success path where no lock or delegation exists copies the open stateid and returns 0, 1058).

name: nfsd_io_cache_read_set
prose: Precondition: data is unused and val is the u64 written to the debugfs file /sys/kernel/debug/nfsd/io_cache_read (nfsd/debugfs.c:58-80, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 or -EINVAL. name: nilfs_dat_prepare_update
prose: Precondition: dat is the DAT metadata inode; oldreq describes the virtual block whose lifetime is to be ended (oldreq->pr_entry_nr valid) and newreq is a request structure for a new virtual block to allocate (its pr_entry_nr is an output of the allocation, not an input) (nilfs2/dat.c:242-255, int). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno through a single 'return ret' at line 254. It first calls nilfs_dat_prepare_end(dat, oldreq): if that fails its error is returned and nothing further is done (prepare_end releases its own entry buffer on its failure paths, but when it fails with -EINVAL after having prepared a free-entry reservation for a never-assigned block it only aborts the entry buffer, not the palloc free preparation, dat.c:177-191). If prepare_end succeeds it calls nilfs_dat_prepare_alloc(dat, newreq); if that returns a negative error, nilfs_dat_abort_end(dat, oldreq) is called to undo the first preparation and the error is returned; on success both preparations (end of the old entry and allocation of the new entry) are held, and the caller must commit or abort them, and 0 is returned.

name: nilfs_store_disk_layout
prose: Precondition: nilfs points to an initialised the_nilfs whose ns_sb and ns_blocksize are set, and sbp is the on-disk superblock (nilfs2/the_nilfs.c:437-527, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 if every check passes (line 526), otherwise -EINVAL; fields of *nilfs are assigned as the checks proceed, so a failing call can leave earlier fields (ns_sbsize, ns_inode_size, ns_first_ino, ns_blocks_per_segment, ns_first_data_block, ns_r_segments_percentage) already overwritten. Return points, in order: -EINVAL with an error message if s_rev_level is below NILFS_MIN_SUPP_REV (448); -EINVAL without any message if s_bytes (ns_sbsize) is greater than BLOCK_SIZE (452); -EINVAL with a message if the inode size exceeds the block size (458), is below NILFS_MIN_INODE_SIZE (462), or if the super-root size for that inode size exceeds the block size (468); -EINVAL with a message if s_first_ino is below NILFS_USER_INO (476), if s_blocks_per_segment is below NILFS_SEG_MIN_BLOCKS (483), if the reserved segments percentage is outside 1..99 (494), if s_nsegments exceeds nilfs_max_segment_count (503), or if the device has a known size (sb_bdev_nr_blocks non-zero) smaller than nsegments * blocks_per_segment (520). On success nilfs_set_nsegments(nilfs, nsegments) (which also sets the number of segments and the derived reserved-segment count) is called and ns_crc_seed is stored before returning 0.

name: uni2char
prose: Precondition: uni is the Unicode value to convert, out points to a writable buffer, boundlen is its size in bytes (nls/nls_cp932.c:7837-7875, static int uni2char(const wchar_t uni, unsigned char *out, int boundlen)). Postcondition: returns the number of bytes written (1 or 2) or a negative errno. Return points: -ENAMETOOLONG at 7845 if boundlen <= 0 (nothing written). If the high byte is 0xFF and the low byte is in 0x61..0x9F it writes the single byte cl + 0x40 to out[0] and returns 1 (7849), without any boundlen check beyond the first one (boundlen >= 1 is already known). Otherwise, if page_uni2charset[ch] is non-NULL: -ENAMETOOLONG at 7854 if boundlen < 2 (nothing written); else it writes out[0], out[1] from the table, returns -EINVAL if both are zero (the two bytes have been written) and otherwise 2. Else (no table for that high byte) if ch == 0: for cl <= 0x7F it writes one byte and returns 1; for cl >= 0xA0 it writes out[0] and out[1] from u2c_00hi without checking boundlen < 2 (so out must be writable for two bytes on this path) and returns 2 only if both bytes are non-zero, otherwise falls to -EINVAL (the two bytes have been written); for 0x80 <= cl < 0xA0 it returns -EINVAL at 7871. Any other high byte with no table returns -EINVAL at 7874.
note: slice cut head (function at 7837-7875, slice 7847-7934). reviewers all right: round 1 (the ch == 0, cl >= 0xA0 path writes two bytes without a boundlen < 2 check, 7865-7869), round 2 (out needs two writable bytes on the table path), round 15 (the 0xFF path returns 1 with no boundlen < 2 test, 7847-7849, which is fine since boundlen >= 1 there, so -ENAMETOOLONG does not apply to it). If that is NULL it returns -EINVAL (line 568) with nothing registered. Otherwise it copies p_nls->charset2upper and p_nls->charset2lower into the static nls_table named table and returns register_nls(&table) (line 565): 0 on success, or the error register_nls returns. name: fanotify_get_response
prose: Precondition: group is the fsnotify group that owns event, event is the fanotify permission event whose state is FAN_EVENT_INIT, FAN_EVENT_REPORTED or answered, and the caller has queued it and is waiting for the userspace answer (fanotify/fanotify.c:224-291, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 if userspace allowed the access, a negative errno otherwise, and (except in one case) the event is destroyed with fsnotify_destroy_event before returning. It waits with wait_event_state until event->state == FAN_EVENT_ANSWERED, in state TASK_KILLABLE|TASK_FREEZABLE, so only a fatal signal ends the wait early (freezing does not); a negative wait result ret (-ERESTARTSYS) is handled under group->notification_lock: if the state is FAN_EVENT_REPORTED (reported to userspace, no answer yet) it is set to FAN_EVENT_CANCELED and ret is returned at line 244 WITHOUT destroying the event (it is freed when userspace answers); if the state is FAN_EVENT_INIT (still queued) the event is removed from the queue; in the remaining case (answered while the signal raced) nothing more is done; in the INIT and ANSWERED cases it goes to out, destroys the event and returns the negative ret. If the wait completed normally, the response is converted: FAN_ALLOW gives 0; FAN_DENY gives -errno when a custom errno is present in the response (fanotify_get_response_errno), else -EPERM; any other response gives -EPERM; if FAN_AUDIT is set in the response audit_fanotify is called. Then the event is destroyed and ret returned (290).
note: slice cut head (function at 224-291, slice 1-260). reviewers: original right (the answered-race returns the negative ret with the event destroyed, 252-258); round 15 right: only TASK_KILLABLE ends the wait early; TASK_FREEZABLE does not (232-234).

name: attr_allocate_frame
prose: Precondition: ni is an NTFS inode with a compressed (extended) unnamed $DATA attribute, the caller holds the inode lock and ni->file.run_lock for writing, frame is the frame number, compr_size the compressed size in bytes of the frame, new_valid a candidate valid size (ntfs3/attrib.c:1655-1877, int attr_allocate_frame(struct ntfs_inode *ni, CLST frame, size_t compr_size, u64 new_valid); the packet name was truncated). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno; the only return is 'return err' at 1876. It finds the base $DATA attribute (-ENOENT at 1671 if missing, returned directly; -EINVAL at 1674 if it is not compressed/sparse (is_attr_ext), returned directly). It locates the attribute segment covering vcn = frame << NTFS_LZNT_CUNIT (-EINVAL if there is no attribute list or no such segment), loads its runs and asks attr_is_frame_compressed how many clusters (clst_data) the frame currently uses (errors go to out). It subtracts that from the total size and computes len = clusters needed for compr_size. If len == clst_data nothing else changes. If len < clst_data it deallocates the surplus clusters (run_deallocate_ex) and replaces them with a sparse run (-ENOMEM if run_add_entry fails); if len > clst_data it allocates more clusters (attr_allocate_clusters, error: out) starting after the last cluster. It then adds the new size back to total_size and repacks the runs (mi_pack_runs; at repack), updates attr_b->nres.total_size, inode bytes, marks the inode and mft record dirty, and if the packed attribute no longer reaches the old end it creates an attribute list when none exists (ni_create_attr_list then re-finds the base attribute and repacks), or merges/removes following attribute segments (mi_remove_attr, al_remove_le (-EINVAL on failure), re-load of the next record, attr_load_runs) and inserts a new non-resident segment (ni_insert_nonresident) for the remainder; on success run_truncate_around is called. There is no undo of an allocation or deallocation already done when a later step fails: errors after the cluster allocation or deallocation go to out leaving the run list and bitmap changes in place. In particular, if ni_load_mi fails at line 1820 the code sets attr = NULL and goes to out with err still holding its previous (zero) value, so the function can return 0 on that failure. At out, if attr_b is set, it clamps new_valid to data_size and, if new_valid differs from the stored valid size, writes the stored valid_size back unchanged (line 1871: it stores le64_to_cpu(attr_b->nres.valid_size), not new_valid) and sets mi_b->dirty.
note: slice cut head (function at 1655-1877, slice 1016-1267 is the middle of an earlier function; the packet slice does not contain it, name outside slice). reviewer round 15 right: no undo path exists after cluster allocation in this version (the failure paths 1703, 1707, 1721, 1725, 1744, 1755, 1776 simply go to out) and ni_load_mi failure at 1820-1823 can return 0. The unchanged-valid_size store at 1871 looks like a defect in the source; reported as the code does it.

name: wnd_find
prose: Precondition: wnd is an initialised NTFS bitmap window (wnd_bitmap) with its extent trees and free-bit counts consistent, to_alloc is the number of bits wanted, hint the preferred start bit, flags is a combination of BITMAP_FIND_FULL and BITMAP_FIND_MARK_AS_USED, allocated is a valid pointer (ntfs3/bitmap.c:959-1301, size_t wnd_find(struct wnd_bitmap *wnd, size_t to_alloc, size_t hint, size_t flags, size_t *allocated)). Postcondition: returns the number of bits found (at line 1297) and stores the first bit of the run in *allocated, or returns 0 (label no_space, line 1300) when nothing suitable was found, in which case *allocated is not written. For BITMAP_FIND_FULL (the whole request wanted): it returns 0 early if the free count (minus the reserved zone) or the cached largest extent is smaller than to_alloc; otherwise to_alloc is first limited to the largest known extent when FULL is not set. A hint inside the reserved zone is moved to zone_end, and a hint >= nbits is reset to 0. If the start tree is empty and the extent cache is up to date it returns 0, else it scans the bitmap. With a hint it looks for a cached extent containing or following the hint: a run starting at hint with enough length (and hint + to_alloc <= nbits) is returned with that length; without FIND_FULL a shorter run at the hint is returned with its shortened length. Otherwise it takes the biggest cached extent: if that is large enough it is used; with FIND_FULL it gives up when the biggest extent is below the original request, otherwise it is used at its own size, so a FIND_FULL result is never below the original request in the extent-tree path except for the clamp 'to_alloc = max_alloc - e->start.key' at 1099-1100, which can return fewer bits than requested even with FIND_FULL; without FIND_FULL the length is the extent size (or, when the cache is not trusted, extended bit by bit while free). If the extent cache cannot decide (nothing big enough, cache not up to date) it scans the bitmap windows from hint to the end and then [0, hint + to_alloc), skipping the reserved zone and windows with no free bits, accumulating the best fragment (b_pos, b_len); a scan hit returns that run, and if none fits, without FIND_FULL it returns the largest fragment found (and updates wnd->extent_max), with FIND_FULL it returns 0. A wnd_map read error for a window is skipped (marked TODO). At found, with BITMAP_FIND_MARK_AS_USED it calls wnd_set_used (failure: return 0), else it may raise wnd->extent_max; then it stores *allocated and returns to_alloc.
note: slice cut head (function at 959-1301, slice 1027-1277). reviewer round 15 right: with BITMAP_FIND_FULL the clamp at bitmap.c:1099-1100 can make the returned length smaller than the requested to_alloc. I describe the bitmap scan path at a summary level; individual conditions in wnd_scan were not read.

name: do_action
prose: Precondition: log is the NTFS log being replayed, oe is the open-attribute entry for the record (oe->ptr is its OpenAttr), lrh the log record header, op the operation code, data/dlen the redo or undo data of that operation, rec_len the log record length and rlsn the LSN of the record being applied (may be NULL) (ntfs3/fslog.c:3103-3842, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno through 'return err' at 3837, plus two earlier returns: -ENOMEM at 3169 if the temporary mft_inode for InitializeFileRecordSegment cannot be allocated, and the error from mi_get / mi_format_new at 3173. It works in two switches. First switch (prepare): for MFT-record operations (InitializeFileRecordSegment through ZeroEndOfFileRecord) it takes the MFT record number rno = vbo >> record_bits, uses a cached inode (ilookup) or reads the record (mi_get; for InitializeFileRecordSegment a failed read is replaced by a freshly formatted record); unless the operation is DeallocateFileRecordSegment it jumps to dirty_vol if the record has the BAAD signature or fails check_file_record, jumps to out WITHOUT any change (err 0) if check_lsn(&rec->rhdr, rlsn) says the record is already newer, and may switch to the child record of the parent inode; for attribute operations (UpdateNonresidentValue, the index-allocation operations, bitmap set/clear operations, UpdateRecordDataAllocation) it allocates buffer_le (-ENOMEM at 3256 is returned directly) and reads the cluster run with ntfs_read_run_nb: a read error goes to out with err set to that error (not to dirty_vol, so the volume is not marked dirty), then applies the fixup for ATTR_ALLOC buffers. Any other op value only triggers WARN_ON(1). Second switch (apply): each operation validates its inputs against the record and attribute sizes and, on any inconsistency, jumps to dirty_vol (sets log->set_dirty = true and falls to out with err unchanged, normally 0, i.e. the function does not return an error for a corrupt log record); for the index-allocation operations an old LSN in the index buffer (check_lsn fails) goes to out leaving everything untouched and err 0. Otherwise it edits the record or buffer in place: initialise/zero/write-end of a file record, create or delete an attribute (shifting the tail, adjusting rec->used, next_attr_id and hard_links), update resident value or mapping pairs, set new attribute sizes, add or delete a root index entry, set a root entry's vcn, update file name or record data in the index root, write bytes in the non-resident value, add or delete an index entry in an allocation buffer, write the end of an index buffer, set a vcn or file name in an allocation entry, set or clear bits in the non-resident bitmap, update record data in an allocation entry; changes to loaded attributes (find_loaded_attr) are mirrored by duplicating the attribute. After the switch, if rlsn is non-NULL it stamps the record and/or index buffer LSN; if the MFT record is dirty it writes it with mi_write (error: out); if a non-resident buffer was changed (a_dirty) it re-applies the fixups where needed and writes it with ntfs_sb_write_run (error: out). out releases the inode (iput) or the mft_inode (mi_put, unless it was the child record) and frees buffer_le, then returns err.
note: slice cut head (function at 3103-3842, slice 3065-3320 covers only the first part). reviewers: original right (check_lsn failure goes to out with err 0 and no change, 3182-3183, 3616-3617 etc.); round 2 wrong (dirty_vol at 3839-3841 sets log->set_dirty and returns the current err, 0 unless already set; it does not set -EINVAL); round 15 right (ntfs_read_run_nb error goes to out at 3258-3261, not dirty_vol). The operation-by-operation detail is summarised, not exhaustive.

name: ntfs_set_state
prose: Precondition: sbi is a mounted NTFS superblock info; dirty is NTFS_DIRTY_CLEAR, NTFS_DIRTY_DIRTY or NTFS_DIRTY_ERROR (ntfs3/fsntfs.c:929-1002). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. Return points: 0 at 944 without any change if sbi->volume.real_dirty is already set or the filesystem is mounted read-only (so for NTFS_DIRTY_ERROR on an already real-dirty or read-only volume real_dirty is not (re)set); 0 at 949 if the requested state equals the cached VOLUME_FLAG_DIRTY bit in sbi->volume.flags (no write; again real_dirty is not set in that case even for NTFS_DIRTY_ERROR); -EINVAL at 953 if sbi->volume.ni is NULL (nothing changed); otherwise under ni->ni_lock it looks up the $Volume ATTR_VOL_INFO attribute: -EINVAL (via out) if it is missing or its resident data is too small, no update. It then sets the on-disk flag: NTFS_DIRTY_ERROR logs a notice, sets sbi->volume.real_dirty = true and falls through to NTFS_DIRTY_DIRTY which sets VOLUME_FLAG_DIRTY; NTFS_DIRTY_CLEAR clears it. If the flags changed, sbi->volume.flags is updated and the mft record marked dirty. After unlocking, an error from the lookup path is returned (line 993) without writing; otherwise it marks the volume inode dirty (mark_inode_dirty_sync) and returns the result of _ni_write_inode(&ni->vfs_inode, 1) (the write is attempted even if the flags did not change).
note: slice cut head (function at 929-1002, slice 760-1011). reviewers: original right (missing attribute or info return -EINVAL without updating, and ni NULL is handled in the function, 951-967); round 2 right (NTFS_DIRTY_ERROR sets real_dirty at 974); round 15 right (the cached-flag check at 947-949 returns 0 before real_dirty is set).

name: indx_delete_entry
prose: Precondition: indx is the index (directory or other index) of inode ni with the inode lock held, key and key_len identify the entry to remove and ctx is the comparison context (ntfs3/index.c:2356-2736, int indx_delete_entry(struct ntfs_index *indx, struct ntfs_inode *ni, const void *key, u32 key_len, const void *ctx)). Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno through the single 'return err' at 2735. Errors: -ENOMEM if either fnd_get fails (2376, 2382) or if the temporary copy of the replacement entry (kmemdup, 2619) fails; -EINVAL if the index root cannot be obtained (indx_get_root, at 2388 and again at 2494 and 2699), if the tree is found corrupt while re-locating the parent entry (2508, 2564, 2576, 2586, 2599), or if resizing the root attribute fails (2709); -ENOENT if the key is not found (not exact match) at 2398; the error of indx_find (2394), of indx_get_entry_to_replace (2447), of indx_insert_into_buffer / indx_insert_into_root (2462), of indx_find_buffer (2529) and of indx_insert_entry (2667). Behaviour: it finds the entry; a leaf entry is removed from the root (shrinking the resident root attribute) or from the index buffer (indx_write); if the buffer becomes an empty leaf the fnd stack records it for branch deletion. An entry with a sub-node pointer is replaced by the in-order successor taken from the subtree (indx_get_entry_to_replace) which is inserted in its place with the old entry's vbn, or, if the subtree has no replacement, the subtree children are freed and the next entry inherits the deleted entry's vbn. When an empty branch was found it then reloads the root, locates the parent chain, and either moves one entry up (a copy 'me' of the first non-empty parent's entry stripped of its sub-node pointer is deleted and re-inserted with indx_insert_entry, freed index buffers are marked free in the bitmap and the index is shrunk (indx_shrink; its result is not checked)), or, if the whole tree is empty, collapses it: the ATTR_ALLOC and ATTR_BITMAP attributes are truncated and removed, the root attribute is resized to an empty leaf and filled with a single last entry; in this collapse branch the results of attr_set_size and ni_remove_attr are assigned to err but only the last assignment matters, so earlier failures there are overwritten, and a failure in the last ni_remove_attr is returned unless the root lookup after it fails. The results of indx_write, indx_mark_free and indx_free_children are ignored. out releases both fnd structures with fnd_put.

name: ntfs_create_inode
prose: Precondition: dir is the parent directory inode (with ntfs_i(dir) and a valid index root), dentry is the new name's dentry, uni the converted UTF-16 name (or NULL), mode the new mode (directory, regular, symlink or special), dev the device number for special files, symname/size the symlink target for S_ISLNK, fnd is a find context if the caller already holds the directory lock, else NULL (ntfs3/inode.c:1194-1726, int ntfs_create_inode(struct mnt_idmap *idmap, struct inode *dir, struct dentry *dentry, const struct cpu_str *uni, umode_t mode, dev_t dev, const char *symname, u32 size, struct ntfs_fnd *fnd); it returns an int, 0 or a negative errno, not an inode pointer). Postcondition: single return 'return err' at 1725; the directory lock is taken (ni_lock_dir) and released at out1 only when fnd is NULL. Steps and errors: -EINVAL (1230) if the directory's index root cannot be obtained; attribute flags fa are chosen by mode (directory attributes inherited from the parent, symlink = reparse point, regular file sparse/compressed/archive, dot-files hidden with the hide_dot_files option, read-only if no write bits); -ENOMEM (1299) if the PATH_MAX directory-entry buffer cannot be allocated; -EINVAL (1305) if the parent inode is bad; -EIO (1310) after a forced shutdown; it marks the volume dirty (ntfs_set_state, result ignored); ntfs_look_free_mft error (1318) and ntfs_new_inode error (1324) unwind via out3/out2; it builds the new MFT record in memory (standard information with the security id, file name from fill_name_de whose error or an invalid Windows name with -EINVAL goes to out4, optional security attribute, then a directory index root, an empty resident data attribute for symlink-to-file or ordinary files, and for symlinks a reparse buffer which is stored resident or in newly allocated clusters; failures of indx_init, ntfs_create_reparse_buffer, attr_allocate_clusters, run_pack, a run length mismatch (-EINVAL), ntfs_sb_write_run or ntfs_insert_reparse unwind via out4/out5); sets the inode operations; with POSIX ACLs enabled it calls ntfs_init_acl (error: out5), and for non-symlinks ntfs_save_wsl_perm (error: out6) and updates the name attribute's extend_data; then indx_insert_entry adds the name to the parent index (error: out6). On success it d_instantiate_new's the inode, sets all timestamps to the creation time on the new inode and the parent, marks both inodes dirty and returns 0 via out2. Failure unwinding: out6 removes a non-resident EA attribute and an inserted reparse entry; out5 deallocates the file's clusters (non-directories); out4 clears the record's in-use bit, clear_nlink, discard_new_inode; out3 marks the MFT record free; out2 frees new_de and rp; out1 unlocks the directory if fnd is NULL.
note: slice cut head (function at 1194-1726, slice 1289-1542 is the middle). reviewer round 15 wrong for this tree: ntfs_create_inode is declared 'int' (inode.c:1194) and returns err at 1725; it does not return an inode pointer (the reviewer may have seen a different kernel version).

name: ntfs_read_mft
prose: Precondition: inode is a newly allocated, locked (I_NEW) NTFS inode from iget_locked with i_ino and i_sb set; name is NULL or the file name the caller expects among the record's names, ref is the MFT reference (with its sequence number) used to reach the record (ntfs3/inode.c:23-508, static struct inode *ntfs_read_mft(struct inode *inode, const struct cpu_str *name, const struct MFT_REF *ref); the packet name was a placeholder). Postcondition: returns the same inode, fully initialised and unlocked with unlock_new_inode, at line 500, or ERR_PTR(err) at 507 after iget_failed(inode); the sbi->mft.ni pointer is cleared in both exits when ino == MFT_REC_MFT and sb->s_root is not yet set. err is never 0 on the failure exit: it is set to -EINVAL at the start of every attribute enumeration step (line 122), so every 'goto out' taken while parsing attributes or after the enumeration ends yields at least -EINVAL unless a more specific value was set. Failure causes: the mi_init or mi_read error (return as is), -ENOMEM if the initial MFT run cannot be added, -EINVAL on a sequence-number mismatch with ref (unless the log is being replayed) or when rec->total differs from the record size, the record is not a base record, a directory with ino MFT_REC_MFT, a malformed attribute (bad name offset, nonresident size fields inconsistent, wrong size for STD info or FILE_NAME, a non-resident or wrongly collated $I30 root, an attribute list with name or nested or in the log file, non-resident or too large MFT bitmap, roff > asize for a run, unpack error), -ESTALE if the record is not in use, the error of ntfs_load_attr_list, indx_init or run_unpack_ex, -EINVAL if no standard-information attribute was found, the inode is bad, there is no non-DOS file name, or the record type is not directory, symlink, regular, special or an entry under $Extend, and -ENOENT if name was given but no matching name was found. On success it records times and attributes from the standard information, the file names (counting hard links; the record's hard_links field is corrected on the fly if it differs and the record is marked dirty), data sizes and runs, directory index, reparse (symlink) info and WSL extended attributes, sets i_mode, nlink, i_op/i_fop/aops by type, the immutable flag if sys_immutable and the system attribute apply, and S_NOSEC if there are no extended attributes.
note: item named 'inode-setup function (tail)'; the slice 256-509 is the tail of ntfs_read_mft (inode.c:23-508; slice cut head). reviewer round 15 wrong: line 122 sets err = -EINVAL at every next_attr iteration, so the goto out paths for ATTR_ROOT non_res (275-276), !std5 (410-411) and is_bad_inode (413-414) return -EINVAL, not 0/NULL; the function returns ERR_PTR(err) or the inode, never NULL. The earlier prose is essentially right and has been rewritten with the full error set.

name: lz_copy
prose: Precondition: dst points into the output buffer, offset is the distance back to the match source (src = dst - offset, which must not underrun the buffer), length is the match length (non-zero; the function's comment says length and offset must already be validated and dst + length must not overrun the buffer), bufend points one past the end of the output buffer, min_length is the minimum match length of the format (2 or 3 or other; ntfs3/lib/decompress_common.h:254-341, static forceinline u8 *lz_copy(u8 *dst, u32 length, u32 offset, const u8 *bufend, u32 min_length); the packet name copy_match does not exist). Postcondition: copies length bytes from dst - offset to dst and returns dst + length (the function writes at most up to bufend, and writes beyond dst + length only by whole words when at least WORDBYTES - 1 bytes remain before bufend). With FAST_UNALIGNED_ACCESS and bufend - (dst + length) >= WORDBYTES - 1: for offset >= WORDBYTES it copies whole words (unaligned) in a loop until dst reaches the end, possibly writing up to WORDBYTES - 1 bytes past dst + length (inside the buffer) and returns end (line 298); for offset == 1 it fills with words of the repeated previous byte the same way and returns end (312); other offsets below WORDBYTES fall through. In all other cases (no FAST_UNALIGNED_ACCESS, near the buffer end, or small offsets other than 1) it copies bytewise: first min_length-related bytes (one if min_length >= 2 and one more if min_length >= 3, each decrementing length), then a do-while loop copying until length reaches 0 (so it needs length >= 1 after those decrements), and returns dst (the advanced pointer, line 340). The overlapping-copy semantics (a match that overlaps its own output) are preserved by the bytewise loop; no other state is touched.
note: item name copy_match does not exist; the code in the slice (259-343) is lz_copy (decompress_common.h:254-341, slice cut head). Mechanical complaint only; contract left empty because of pointer arguments and the memory writes.

name: ntfs_fill_super
prose: Precondition: sb is a super_block with s_fs_info set to the ntfs_sb_info and an open block device; fc is the fs_context whose fs_private holds the mount options (ntfs3/super.c:1232-1708, static int). Postcondition: returns 0 on success (line 1695, with sb->s_root set) or a negative errno at 1707 after cleanup. Early returns without cleanup via out: -EINVAL at 1258 if fc->fs_private is NULL ('missing mount options'), -ENOMEM at 1262 or 1268 if the options copy or the nls name copy fails. Otherwise it copies the options into sbi->options, sets superblock operations, loads the nls table (an error pointer gives -EINVAL, via out), records the device discard granularity, and calls ntfs_init_from_boot (error: out; it may return a backup boot sector in boot2). It then loads, in order, $Volume (ntfs_iget5 error: out; a missing or too small ATTR_VOL_INFO, or one that is an extended attribute: -EINVAL via put_inode_out; the volume flags are stored and VOLUME_FLAG_DIRTY sets volume.real_dirty), $MFTMirr, $LogFile (ntfs_loadlog_and_replay error: put_inode_out), then: -EINVAL if log replay is still needed and the mount is read-write; -EINVAL if the volume flag is dirty on a read-write mount and options->force is not set (the force option avoids this failure); $MFT (wnd_init and ni_load_all_mi errors: put_inode_out), $Bitmap (size and bitmap checks: -EINVAL, wnd_init error), ntfs_refresh_zone, $BadClus (each bad run is marked used in the bitmap on read-write mounts; a bitmap inconsistency marks the volume NTFS_DIRTY_ERROR), $AttrDef (size between one and 100 entries else -EINVAL; allocation -ENOMEM; read error; first entry must be ATTR_STD; entries are accepted while ascending and aligned), $UpCase (size must be 0x10000 * sizeof(short), else -EINVAL; read error; the table may be replaced by a shared copy), and for NTFS 3.x volumes (is_ntfs3) $Secure (ntfs_security_init error: out) and the $Extend, $Reparse and $ObjId parts (their failures only log a warning and continue to load_root). It loads the root inode (error: out; -EINVAL if its i_op is not set), d_make_root (-ENOMEM on failure, put_inode_out), writes back the backup boot block over the primary one when boot2 was used, creates the procfs directory, and sets SB_RDONLY for legacy NTFS. put_inode_out does iput(inode) and falls into out, which puts the mount options, calls ntfs3_put_sbi and frees boot2, then returns err. Several error paths reached via out leave the inode references taken for earlier metadata files (such as $MFTMirr) already released, but the sbi cleanup is done by ntfs3_put_sbi in out.

name: o2hb_send_nego_msg
prose: Precondition: key and type identify an o2net message type/key pair, target is the destination node number and node_num is the sender node number placed in the message (ocfs2/cluster/heartbeat.c:396-412, static int). Postcondition: has one return, 'return ret' at 411. It fills a local struct o2hb_nego_msg with node_num and calls o2net_send_message(type, key, &msg, sizeof(msg), target, &status); while that call returns -EAGAIN or -ENOMEM it sleeps 100 ms (msleep) and sends again, so it does not return for those two values (it can loop indefinitely if they persist). The final ret is the value of o2net_send_message for any other outcome: 0 on success, or another negative errno; the remote handler's reply status written into the local 'status' variable is not examined and not returned.

name: o2net_listen_data_ready
prose: Precondition: sk is the TCP socket whose data_ready callback this is; the caller does not hold sk->sk_callback_lock (the function takes it itself with read_lock_bh) (ocfs2/cluster/tcp.c:2010-2046, static void). Postcondition: returns nothing. It reads sk->sk_user_data into ready under the read lock. If it is NULL (teardown race) ready is set to sk->sk_data_ready. Otherwise, if sk->sk_state == TCP_LISTEN it queues o2net_listen_work on o2net_wq and keeps ready (the original data_ready saved in sk_user_data); if the socket is in any other state (a child socket still carrying the inherited callback) ready is set to NULL. After read_unlock_bh, if ready is non-NULL it is called with sk, so for a listening socket and for the teardown-race case the previous data_ready is invoked after the lock is dropped; for a non-listening socket nothing is called.
note: slice cut head (function at 2010-2046, slice 1768-2022). reviewers: original right (the function takes sk_callback_lock itself, 2016/2043); round 15 right (the TCP_LISTEN path still calls ready(sk) after the unlock, 2036-2045).

name: dlm_convert_lock_handler
prose: Precondition: msg is an o2net message carrying a struct dlm_convert_lock, len its length, data is the dlm_ctxt of the domain, ret_data unused here (ocfs2/dlm/dlmconvert.c:429-555, int dlm_convert_lock_handler(struct o2net_msg *msg, u32 len, void *data, void **ret_data); the packet name dlmconvert is not a function in this file). Postcondition: returns an enum dlm_status as int: DLM_REJECTED at 444 if dlm_grab(dlm) fails (nothing else done, no reference to drop); otherwise status is one of DLM_IVBUFLEN (name length above DLM_LOCKID_NAME_MAX), DLM_BADARGS (both LKM_PUT_LVB and LKM_GET_LVB set), DLM_IVLOCKID (no such lock resource, or the lock cookie/node is not found on the resource's granted queue), the status of __dlm_lockres_state_to_status(res) when the resource is not in a normal state (at 476, before the lock search), the status of the conversion __dlmconvert_master, or DLM_NORMAL, returned through 'return status' at 554. After the lookup of the lock on the granted queue (a reference is taken on it with dlm_lock_get), it records the LVB request in lksb->flags (BUG_ON if the flags are already set) and copies the LVB for a put. Then under res->spinlock it re-reads the resource state; if DLM_NORMAL it reserves an AST (__dlm_lockres_reserve_ast), sets DLM_LOCK_RES_IN_PROGRESS, calls __dlmconvert_master(dlm, res, lock, flags, cnv->requested_type, &call_ast, &kick_thread), clears IN_PROGRESS and wakes res->wq; if the final status is not DLM_NORMAL it logs dlm_error (not for DLM_NOTQUEUED) and clears the LVB flags in lksb. At leave it drops the lock reference (if one was taken), queues the AST (dlm_queue_ast) when call_ast was set or else releases the reserved AST (dlm_lockres_release_ast) when one was reserved, kicks the dlm thread if requested, drops the lockres reference (if looked up) and the dlm reference (dlm_put), then returns the status. The reference counts on dlm, res and lock are taken by this function itself and dropped before it returns on every path after dlm_grab succeeded.
note: item was named dlmconvert and marked dropped; the real function is dlm_convert_lock_handler (dlmconvert.c:429-555) and the slice 514-555 is its tail (slice cut head); FIXED per rule 6. The earlier prose assumed the caller held references on dlm, res and lock and then dropped them; in the code the handler takes its own references (dlm_grab at 442, dlm_lookup_lockres at 469, dlm_lock_get at 486) and the caller holds none.

name: dlm_is_host_down
prose: Precondition: none; errno is any int (callers pass negative errno values) (ocfs2/dlm/dlmmaster.c:115-137, int dlm_is_host_down(int errno)). Postcondition: returns 1 at line 134 if errno equals one of -EBADF, -ECONNREFUSED, -ENOTCONN, -ECONNRESET, -EPIPE, -EHOSTDOWN, -EHOSTUNREACH, -ETIMEDOUT, -ECONNABORTED, -ENETDOWN, -ENETUNREACH, -ENETRESET, -ESHUTDOWN, -ENOPROTOOPT or -EINVAL (the last meaning, per the source comment, that the tcp code found no socket), and 0 at line 136 for every other value, including 0 and positive values. The function reads and writes no state.

name: dlm_get_lock_resource
prose: Precondition: dlm is a joined dlm_ctxt, lockid is a non-NULL lock name of length namelen (BUG_ON if NULL), flags may contain LKM_LOCAL; the caller holds no dlm->spinlock (ocfs2/dlm/dlmmaster.c:701-996, struct dlm_lock_resource *dlm_get_lock_resource(struct dlm_ctxt *dlm, const char *lockid, int namelen, int flags); the packet name dlm_master_lookup is not the function in this slice). Postcondition: returns a lock resource with a reference held for the caller and an inflight reference, or NULL; single return at 995 (via the labels leave and wake_waiters). The NULL result happens only when allocating the master list entry (kmem_cache_alloc, line 788) or the new lock resource (dlm_new_lockres, line 791) fails; both then go to leave, which frees an unused alloc_mle. It loops at 'lookup': under dlm->spinlock it looks the name up in the hash; if found it takes the resource lock and, if the resource has been unhashed meanwhile, or its owner is unknown (waits for mastering to finish), or it is being dropped (DLM_LOCK_RES_DROPPING_REF, waits), it drops it and restarts the lookup; otherwise it grabs an inflight reference, and if the caller had pre-allocated its own resource it removes that one from the tracking list and puts it (an error log if it was not on the list), and returns the found resource (this path does not touch DLM_LOCK_RES_IN_PROGRESS). If nothing is found and no resource was allocated yet, it allocates alloc_mle and a new resource and restarts the lookup. With the new resource and LKM_LOCAL it sets the owner to this node, inserts it in the hash, grabs an inflight reference and goes to wake_waiters (clears DLM_LOCK_RES_IN_PROGRESS and wakes res->wq). Otherwise it checks the master list: an existing block entry that is a migration or already has a master makes it retry (dropping its references, sleeping 100 ms for a migration); an existing master-type entry for a nonexistent lock BUG()s; with no entry it uses alloc_mle as a DLM_MLE_MASTER entry and records whether a node still needs recovery. It inserts the resource in the hash, grabs an inflight reference, takes an extra reference on the mle, drops the locks, waits for pending recovery (for the $RECOVERY lock it calls dlm_pre_master_reco_lockres), then (unless blocked) sends master requests to the nodes in the vote map with dlm_do_master_request, and waits with dlm_wait_for_lock_mastery; a negative result redoes the request (counting tries, logging after 20). When the master is known it detaches and puts the mle (and the extra reference), asserts res->owner != O2NM_MAX_NODES with BUG_ON, then at wake_waiters clears DLM_LOCK_RES_IN_PROGRESS under res->spinlock and wakes the waiters.
note: item named dlm_master_lookup; the code in the slice (765-1036) is the middle of dlm_get_lock_resource (dlmmaster.c:701-996; slice cut head); renamed, per rule 6. Earlier prose claimed the result always has IN_PROGRESS cleared; on the found-in-hash path (766-779) the flag is not touched, so that claim was too strong and has been removed.
